chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about joining two Surahs in the obligatory and voluntary prayers. He said, 'There is no harm.' And regarding splitting a Surah, he said, 'I dislike that, but there is no harm with it in the voluntary prayer.' And regarding the two Rak'ahs in which the Imam remains silent: is Al-Fatihah recited in them when he is an Imam to be followed? He said, 'If you recite, there is no harm, and if you remain silent, there is no harm.'

Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: His saying (peace be upon him) 'There is no harm' regarding joining two Surahs in the obligatory prayer is interpreted to mean that if one of the two Surahs is Al-Fatihah. And it is not apparent in the text that there is no harm in reciting both after reciting Al-Fatihah. And if that is not apparent in its text, we interpret it according to what we said, so as not to contradict what we have previously presented from the narrations.

key_terms.إِمَامٌ يُقْتَدَى بِهِ: An Imam to be followed (leading congregational prayer)
key_terms.الْقِرَانُ: Joining two Surahs in a single Rak'ah
key_terms.تَبْعِيضُ السُّورَةِ: Splitting a single Surah into parts
key_terms.يَصْمُتُ فِيْهِمَا الإِمَامُ: The Imam remains silent (recites quietly) in them

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on joining two Surahs or splitting one Surah in Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in recitation practices, permitting the joining of two Surahs in obligatory prayers and the splitting of a single Surah in voluntary ones. It further establishes that in the silent Fajr Rak'ahs, both the Imam's silence and the follower's recitation are valid, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in ritual worship. The commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan contextualizes the ruling on joining Surahs, ensuring it aligns with broader jurisprudential evidence.
